solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Speaking French well during cameo briefly affected atmosphere

indicators.note: during means one piece sits in the middle of the other while it happens
affected in the sense of put on or contorted, so the letters are rearranged
briefly means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: the French word for well is bien

explanation.surface: Someone's French, spoken during a short film cameo, was put on and stilted, which coloured the whole mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' trims cameo to CAME; 'affected' rearranges that to AMCE; 'during' puts BIEN inside it, AM-BIEN-CE.
explanation.definitionFit: The ambience of a place is its mood or atmosphere, a direct synonym borrowed from French.

clue.text: Time of year gold mine oddly limits workers?

indicators.note: limits means the outer pieces bound the inner one on both sides

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: oddly means the first and third letters are taken

parts.note: TU stands for trade union, a body of workers

explanation.surface: A gold mine seems to restrict its workers in a curious way for part of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limits' means gold and the odd letters of mine sit on either side of the workers' union; 'oddly' takes letters one and three of mine.
explanation.definitionFit: Fall, as Americans call it, is the season after summer, a time of year.

clue.text: Academic individual probes unusual element

parts.note: BA, a Bachelor of Arts, is an academic

indicators.note: probes means the piece goes inside the other

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or unusual
I is a single one, an individual

explanation.surface: A scholar investigates an unusual chemical element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'probes' puts the individual inside the unusual piece; rum meaning odd is a British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Barium is a metallic chemical element, atomic number 56, used in X-ray meals.

clue.text: With little energy, Roger avoids training duty

indicators.note: avoids means these letters are left out of the word

parts.note: exercise is physical training
E is the physics abbreviation for energy
R is radio shorthand for roger, message received

explanation.surface: Roger is low on energy and dodges his training session.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing ER from EXERCISE leaves the tax word.
explanation.definitionFit: Excise is a tax charged on goods such as alcohol and tobacco, so a duty.

clue.text: Extremely charming absorbing play written by competent film star

indicators.note: written by in a down light means placed beneath, so this piece follows
absorbing means the outer pieces take the other into themselves
extremely means the first and last letters of the word

parts.note: a lark is a bit of fun or play
able means capable or competent

explanation.surface: A charming, capable actor absorbs himself in a play he wrote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' takes only the ends of charming, 'absorbing' wraps them round the play, and 'written by' in a down light places competent below. He starred in Gone with the Wind.
explanation.definitionFit: This actor was a leading Hollywood movie star of the 1930s and 1940s.

clue.text: China devotee collects the ultimate in Worcester

indicators.note: collects means the first piece gathers the other inside itself

parts.note: a fiend is an enthusiast or devotee, as in a fresh-air fiend

indicators.note: the ultimate in a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A collector of porcelain picks up the finest piece of Royal Worcester china.
explanation.walkthrough: China is capitalised to look like the country or porcelain; it is rhyming slang, china plate = mate. 'collects' puts R, the last letter of Worcester, inside FIEND.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang china (plate) means mate, a pal or companion.

clue.text: Radical youth argued fervently on street

indicators.note: fervently suggests the letters are worked up and stirred about

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road, taken here as a street

explanation.surface: A young militant argued passionately out on the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fervently' rearranges argued to REDGUA, then RD. These were the young militants of Mao's Cultural Revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Guards were radical young activists of China's Cultural Revolution, so a member is a radical youth.

clue.text: Average English river, when moving east, becomes huge

indicators.note: moving means the letter is lifted out and put elsewhere in the word

parts.note: the norm is the average or standard
the Ouse is a river in England, in Yorkshire and elsewhere
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: An ordinary English river, when it flows eastward, swells to an enormous size.
explanation.walkthrough: NORM plus OUSE makes NORMOUSE; 'moving' takes its E from the end to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Something vast in size is gigantic or immense, a straight synonym for huge.

clue.text: Checked extent of the rules, filling in legal document

indicators.note: filling in means the pieces go inside the other one

parts.note: a deed is a legal document

indicators.note: the extent of a word is taken as its two ends

parts.note: R stands for rule, so two of them are RR

explanation.surface: A lawyer checks how far the rules reach by filling in a legal form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filling in' puts the pieces inside the legal document; 'extent of' for the two ends of a word is unusual, as the blog's commenters noted.
explanation.definitionFit: To be deterred is to be checked or held back from acting, a past-tense synonym.

clue.text: Appearance that may be made by a sewer rat

parts.note: a turn is a performer's appearance on stage, a music-hall act

parts.words: that may be made by a sewer
parts.note: a sewer here is one who sews, a tailor, who might make a jacket or overcoat

explanation.surface: A creature emerges from the drains of a city's sewer system.
explanation.walkthrough: Sewer suggests a drain, but it is someone who sews; a rat is someone who betrays their side.
explanation.definitionFit: To rat is to desert or betray, and a rat is a traitor who switches sides.

clue.text: Ingenious medic that ends voodoo in middle of Haiti

indicators.note: in means the medic piece is placed inside the other
middle of means the letters of the word left once its ends are removed

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor, a medic

indicators.note: ends points to the final letter of voodoo

explanation.surface: A clever doctor puts an end to voodoo practice in the heart of Haiti.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that ends' takes only the last letter of voodoo, and 'in' places the medic and that letter inside the heart of Haiti.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means skilful and clever with hands or mind, so ingenious is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Reduced dessert or main course?

indicators.note: reduced means the word is shortened by losing a letter at its end

parts.note: a mousse is a light whipped dessert
aka, also known as, introduces an alternative name, just as or can

explanation.surface: A menu question: should a cut-down pudding be taken as dessert, or is it a main?
explanation.walkthrough: MOUSSE loses its last letter to make MOUSS, then AKA; the question mark marks the definition as one example of a main course.
explanation.definitionFit: This Greek baked dish of aubergine and minced meat is served as a main course, an example of one.

clue.text: Seabird sounding resonant some days

indicators.note: sounding means the word is said aloud and its sound is used

parts.note: a resonant voice is full and rich
MAR is the abbreviation for March, a month and so some days

explanation.surface: A seabird whose cry sounds rich and resonant on certain days.
explanation.definitionFit: The fulmar is a grey and white seabird of the petrel family found in northern seas.

clue.text: A day in retreat by river banks — perfect for Mark Twain perhaps

indicators.note: by means the pieces sit next to each other
in retreat means going backwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: MON is the abbreviation for Monday, a day

indicators.note: banks means the river's letters border the other piece on each side

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
plum means first-rate, as in a plum job

explanation.surface: A day spent retreating beside a river makes perfect material for Mark Twain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retreat' turns the day backwards and 'banks' makes the river border the perfect piece. Mark Twain was Samuel Clemens's pen name, so he is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain was the pseudonym of Samuel Clemens, an example of a writer's assumed name.

clue.text: High-flyer drinking French wine somewhere in LA

parts.note: a bat is a flying mammal
on, as in on the bottle, means drinking
rouge is French for red, as in red wine

explanation.surface: A frequent flyer sips red wine somewhere in Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: LA suggests Los Angeles; here it is Louisiana, the US state, whose capital this city is.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the state capital of Louisiana, abbreviated LA, so a place within it.

clue.text: Legendary runner active in Olympic venue

indicators.note: in means the letter is placed within the city name

parts.note: the US city of Atlanta hosted the 1996 Olympic Games
A is the grammar abbreviation for active

explanation.surface: A legendary athlete is active at an Olympic venue.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside the city name after AT; she was the fleet-footed huntress of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this huntress was a famous swift runner, beaten only by golden apples.

clue.text: Prepares for sports event with rowing crew short — something wrong

indicators.note: short means the word lacks its last letter

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen
a sin is a wrongdoing

explanation.surface: Preparing for a race with a rowing crew short of a member would be a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: EIGHT loses its last letter to make EIGH.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxers and jockeys are weighed before a contest, which is how they get ready for an event.

clue.text: Tattoo peculiar on the outside and inside

indicators.note: one sense of the word wraps the other, which sits inside it

parts.note: droll means oddly amusing or peculiar
rum is British slang for odd or peculiar

explanation.surface: A tattoo that is odd both on the surface and underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: The one word peculiar gives two synonyms, one wrapped round the other. Tattoo here is a rapid drumbeat, not ink on skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattoo is a rhythmic beating of drums, such as a military signal, so a rapid roll.

clue.text: In that position around piano, loud duet regularly cited poem

indicators.note: around means the first piece wraps the second

parts.note: there means in that place or position
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: In a recital, a pianist and singer give a loud duet, followed by a quoted poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' wraps the position word round piano and 'regularly' takes every other letter of loud duet. Wordsworth's autobiographical long poem has this title.
explanation.definitionFit: Wordsworth's long autobiographical work is a classic example of a poem in English.

clue.text: Heavyweight retains number one position — master of the canvas?

indicators.note: retains means the first piece holds the second within it

parts.note: a titan is a giant or heavyweight figure
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A heavyweight boxer keeps the number one spot, master of the canvas floor.
explanation.walkthrough: Canvas suggests the boxing ring; the Venetian Renaissance painter is a master of the painted canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: Titian was a great Venetian painter, so an old master working on canvas.

clue.text: Herbal tea given by couple around hospital

indicators.note: around means the first piece wraps the second

parts.note: to tie is to join or couple
san is short for sanatorium, a kind of hospital

explanation.surface: A couple brings herbal tea to a patient in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts the hospital inside the couple; san for a sanatorium is chiefly British.
explanation.definitionFit: A tisane is an infusion of herbs or flowers, the French name for a herbal tea.

clue.text: Committed one with heritage group repeatedly embraces earth

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: embraces means the pieces hold the other between them
repeatedly means the piece appears twice

parts.note: NT is the National Trust, the British heritage conservation body

explanation.surface: A committed member of a heritage group keeps embracing the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: NTNT holds E between its copies. The National Trust looks after historic houses and land in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Being set on doing something is being committed or determined, an adjectival synonym.

clue.text: Swimmer holds dial, looking over pulse

indicators.note: looking over in a down light reads backwards here as the whole piece is turned
holds means the first word contains the second

parts.note: an eel is a swimming fish
dial and mug are both slang for a face

explanation.surface: A swimmer holding a dial checks the pulse on their watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' puts the face inside the swimmer, giving EMUGEL, and 'looking over' turns that whole run round.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulses are edible seeds such as peas, beans and lentils, the plant family's crop.

clue.text: Perseus initially comes across no aid, slaying snaky creature

indicators.note: comes across is taken as one piece lying across the inside of the other
slaying, killing, signals the letters are destroyed and rearranged

parts.note: the setter takes a Greek letter as the initial of the Greek hero Perseus; strictly his name begins with pi

explanation.surface: Perseus, hero of legend, gets no help as he slays a snake-haired Gorgon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slaying' turns NO AID into ODIAN and PHI goes inside, O-PHI-DIAN. Bloggers found this one uneasy: Greek Perseus begins with pi, so the Greek letter is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Ophidian refers to snakes, from the Greek for serpent, so a snaky creature is a snake.

clue.text: One fails to attend food centre in town

parts.note: nosh is slang for food

indicators.note: centre in means the middle letters of the word

explanation.surface: Someone missing a meal in the town centre fails to show up.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-show is a person who books or is expected but does not turn up.

clue.text: Country celebrity Ireland and America rejected earlier

indicators.note: earlier means this piece goes before the other
rejected means turned back, so the pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: US is the abbreviation for the United States of America
a name is a famous person, a big name

explanation.surface: A star whom Ireland and America both turned down was earlier sent to another country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns Ireland and America back as one run, SURI, and 'earlier' sets it before the celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Suriname is a small nation on the north coast of South America, a former Dutch colony.

clue.text: Rings Sally (at baker's) back in road

indicators.note: in means the reversed piece is placed within the road

parts.note: the A1 is Britain's longest numbered road; with the digit 1 read as I it gives AI

indicators.note: back means the piece is read in reverse

parts.note: a Sally Lunn is a sweet bun sold at the baker's, originally from Bath

explanation.surface: Sally, seen at the baker's, walks back along the road wearing rings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the bun's name to NNUL and 'in' sets it inside the road. A Sally Lunn is a large rich teacake from Bath in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Annuli is the Latin plural of annulus, a ring-shaped figure or part.

clue.text: Check Valerie and Stuart both vacated place in office again

parts.note: to rein is to check or restrain, as a horse

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, leaving only the outer letters of each name

explanation.surface: Valerie and Stuart have both left their posts, so someone checks whether to fill the office again.
explanation.walkthrough: Emptying Valerie and Stuart leaves VE and ST.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest is to install formally in office, so doing so a second time fits this.
